gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's 2026 MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) supports only one external display and only one of its two USB-C ports carries video. So no dual-monitor KVM dock, whether it uses one cable or two, can give it two extended screens, and TESmart's HDC202-X24 page names the Neo among the Macs it can't extend to two displays.
standout_why: I compared against both cited rivals and four top results. racksandwatts.com (cited) says only 'On macOS, the MST route gives duplicated external screens' for the iDock C10. tesmart.com's 2026 buying guide (cited) says only that 'Some Apple Silicon MacBooks support only one external display without using DisplayLink' and names no chip. byrdpilot.com says USB-C KVMs give a Mac one extended screen plus a mirror. officekithq.com says 'macOS mirrors rather than extends'. theofficejournal.com and workstationrelay.com make no Mac statements. None of them names a chip, the MacBook Neo, the two-port requirement of dual-cable docks like the iDock M10, or the M3 lid-closed condition.
decides: The finding splits the Mac pick by chip. M4/M5 or Pro/Max MacBooks with two free USB-C/Thunderbolt ports should get the AV Access iDock M10 ($289.99), or the TESmart HDC202-X24 ($699, stock unclear) for one cable. Base M3 owners get two screens only with the lid closed. M1/M2 and MacBook Neo owners should buy a single-monitor KVM, because any dual-monitor dock will only mirror or give them one screen. The KD-E10 and TESmert T722 suit Windows laptops, not Macs. For a Neo, ChatGPT's TESmert T722 and TESmart HDMI 2.1 cards are the wrong buy. Our page needs a 'MacBook Neo / base M1–M2: one screen only' row or note.

findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 4K at 60 Hz (built-in display stays on)
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Supports one external display with up to a native resolution of 4K at 60Hz; Simultaneously supports the built-in display at full native resolution'.

findings.label: Video-capable USB-C ports
findings.value: 1 of 2: the USB 3 (10 Gb/s) USB-C port carries DisplayPort 1.4 (HBR3); the second USB-C port is USB 2 (480 Mb/s) with charging only
findings.note: Apple lists DisplayPort only under the USB 3 port. So the iDock M10's second USB-C cable would get no video from a Neo.

findings.label: Mac chips that get two extended displays
findings.value: M4/M5 or any Pro/Max: two extended. Base M3: two only in clamshell mode (lid closed), mirrored with the lid open. Base M1/M2 and Intel MacBooks: one external display only
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock M10 KVM Docking Station for MacBook
findings.note: From the maker's product page and FAQ. The FAQ chip list names M1–M4 Pro/Max and M3/M4 but leaves out M5, while the headline claim includes M5. The page doesn't mention the MacBook Neo.

findings.label: Laptop ports needed and stated exclusions
findings.value: 'Two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports are required on the MacBook for dual extended displays.' Not compatible with a MacBook + Windows laptop setup. If the second computer is a Mac mini or Mac Studio, both Macs need a Pro chip or M3 or later
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock M10 KVM Docking Station for MacBook
findings.note: Comes with a dual USB-C to dual USB-C cable (USB 3.2 Gen 2, 0.8 m). Desktop input is 1× HDMI + 1× DP, and the HDMI 2.0 and DP 1.2a cables are included.

findings.label: Charging, resolution and price
findings.value: 100 W to the MacBook; dual 4K@60Hz 4:4:4; ultrawide up to 3440×1440@60Hz (5120×1440 drops to 3840×1080); $289.99 list
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock M10 KVM Docking Station for MacBook
findings.note: The dock's power adapter is rated DC 20 V / 6 A. The price is the list price shown on the maker's US page.

findings.label: Port requirement and Macs that can't extend to two displays
findings.value: Needs Thunderbolt 3 or later on PC1 (TB3/4/5). The maker says these can't run dual extended displays over one cable: base M1/M2 MacBook Air/Pro; base M3 (one display with the lid open, two with the lid closed and the power adapter connected); M1 Mac mini; MacBook Neo (A18 Pro); 24-inch iMac (M1, 2021). 'All other Macs can run dual extended displays'
findings.note: This is the only maker document I found that names the MacBook Neo as an exclusion. Its exclusion list doesn't mention base M4.

findings.label: Charging, resolution, price
findings.value: 60 W PD on PC1 only (PC2 gets no charging); each HDMI output up to 3840×2160@60Hz 4:4:4, also 2560×1440@120Hz and 1920×1080@240Hz; $699.00
findings.note: The stock status contradicts itself: the page shows both 'only 6 items left in stock' and a 'Sold Out - Notify me' button.

findings.label: Mac display mode and laptop requirement
findings.value: Mirrored on a MacBook, extended on a Windows laptop. The USB-C input sends two 4K@60Hz streams over DP MST, and 'MacOS doesn't support USB-C MST, so external monitors will show duplicate content'
findings.source_title: AV Access KD-E10 KVM Switch Docking Station
findings.note: Elsewhere the product page says Mac users can 'make full use' of their screens, which contradicts the spec table's 'Mirrored' entry. The spec table is more specific, so I went with it.

findings.label: Laptop charging condition and price
findings.value: Up to 100 W PD 'when connected to a power adapter'. The bundled adapter is 12 V / 3 A, and the page says 'When charging your laptop, please additionally use your laptop's original adapter'. Price $169.99
findings.source_title: AV Access KD-E10 KVM Switch Docking Station
findings.note: 12 V × 3 A = 36 W, so the bundled adapter alone can't supply the 100 W charging figure. A shopper needs to plug the laptop's own charger into the dock.

findings.label: macOS cabling requirement
findings.value: 'macOS uses SST mode and requires connections to both "MST+USB" and "DP Alt" ports for the USB-C computer.' So a Mac needs two USB-C cables, while Windows can use MST through the one 'MST+USB' port. 100 W charging on PC1
findings.source_title: USB-C KVM Switch Buying Guide for Laptop-Based Workstations – TESmert
findings.note: This is the maker's own guide (rank 6 in ChatGPT's results, not cited). It names no Mac chips, so the M1/M2/Neo one-display limits from Apple and the dock makers above still apply.

unsourced: StarTech SV221HUC4K (ChatGPT's $60.99 card): I looked for the DP Alt Mode requirement on the USB-C host and whether it charges the laptop. The startech.com page returned only navigation, and the Farnell datasheet PDF timed out, so I have only search snippets and used none of them.

AV Access KD-E10 and iDock M10 user manual PDFs: both downloaded, but I couldn't extract the text in this environment, so the manuals' notes and exclusions aren't cross-checked against the product pages.

Apple's own per-model display-support pages for the base M3/M4/M5 MacBook Air/Pro (lid-closed rules): support.apple.com/en-us/101571 only links to the per-model pages, and I didn't open them. The chip limits above come from the AV Access and TESmart product pages.

TESmart HDC203-PM24 (DisplayLink, triple 4K60, 100 W PD per the TESmart guide's image filename): I didn't open its product page, so I can't say whether DisplayLink gets a MacBook Neo or a base M1/M2 past the one-display limit.
TESmert T722 price and Mac chip list: I didn't open its product page.
TESmart HDMI 2.1 gaming KVM from ChatGPT's $359 card: I didn't identify the exact model or open its page to check whether the laptop needs native HDMI out.
